prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

They flee from me that sometime did me seek With naked foot, stalking in my chamber. I have seen them gentle, tame, and meek, That now are wild and do not remember That sometime they put themself in danger To take bread at my hand; and now they range, Busily seeking with a continual change. Thanked be fortune it hath been otherwise Twenty times better; but once in special, In thin array after a pleasant guise, When her loose gown from her shoulders did fall, And she me caught in her arms long and small; Therewithall sweetly did me kiss And softly said, “Dear heart, how like you this?” It was no dream: I lay broad waking. But all is turned thorough my gentleness Into a strange fashion of forsaking; And I have leave to go of her goodness, And she also, to use newfangleness. But since that I so kindly am served I would fain know what she hath deserved.

prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: They, With, That

outputs.L1:
They flee from me who once did seek me out,  
With naked feet, stalking within my chamber.  
I have seen them gentle, tame, and meek,  
Who now are wild and no longer remember  
That once they put themselves in danger  
To take bread from my hand; now they range,  
Busily seeking, ever prone to change.

Thanks be to fortune, it has been otherwise—  
Twenty times better, and once especially:  
In a light array, fashioned pleasantly,  
Her loose gown falling from her shoulders,  
She caught me in her slender, lingering arms,  
Sweetly kissed me, and softly said,  
“Dear heart, how do you like this?”

It was no dream: I lay fully awake.  
Yet all, through my gentleness, has turned  
Into a strange manner of forsaking.  
By her grace, I am granted leave to go,  
While she, too, is free to pursue novelty.  
But since I have been served so kindly,  
I would gladly know what she has deserved.
outputs.L2:
Those who once pursued me now run away,  
Barefoot, moving quietly through my room.  
I knew them when they were mild, obedient, and tender;  
Now they have grown untamed and forgotten  
How they once risked approaching me  
To eat bread directly from my hand.  
Instead, they roam restlessly, always searching for something new.

I thank fortune that matters were different before—  
Better on at least twenty occasions, and especially once.  
A woman, lightly dressed in a pleasing manner,  
Let her loose gown slip down from her shoulders.  
She embraced me with her long, slender arms,  
Kissed me sweetly, and whispered,  
“My dear, how do you like this?”

This truly happened; I was fully awake.  
Yet my kindness has transformed everything  
Into an unfamiliar kind of abandonment.  
Through her generosity, I have been granted permission to leave,  
While she is free to pursue novelty as well.  
Since I have been treated with such courtesy,  
I would very much like to know what treatment she deserves.
outputs.L3: The speaker mourns the change in the women who once pursued him eagerly but have now grown distant and seem to have forgotten their former affection. He remembers a time when they were gentle, trusting, and willing to enter his company, whereas now they roam elsewhere, constantly seeking new experiences and relationships. One memory remains especially vivid: a woman loosely dressed took him in her arms, kissed him, and softly asked how he liked the encounter. The speaker firmly insists that this intimate moment was real and not a dream. Yet the tenderness and courtesy he showed her have been repaid with rejection and abandonment. He closes in a tone of bitterness and wounded pride, wondering what treatment the woman now deserves after leaving him behind in pursuit of novelty.
outputs.L4:
### “They Flee from Me”  
*Sir Thomas Wyatt*

They flee from me that sometime did me seek  
With naked foot, stalking in my chamber.  
I have seen them gentle, tame, and meek,  
That now are wild and do not remember  
That sometime they put themself in danger  
To take bread at my hand; and now they range,  
Busily seeking with a continual change.

Thanked be fortune it hath been otherwise  
Twenty times better; but once in special,  
In thin array after a pleasant guise,  
When her loose gown from her shoulders did fall,  
And she me caught in her arms long and small;  
Therewithal sweetly did me kiss,  
And softly said, “Dear heart, how like you this?”

It was no dream: I lay broad waking.  
But all is turned through my gentleness  
Into a strange fashion of forsaking;  
And I have leave to go of her goodness,  
And she also, to use newfangleness.  
But since that I so kindly am served,  
I would fain know what she hath deserved.
outputs.L5: They arrived with the dawn, carrying stories that had waited years to be told. With every step, the silence grew lighter. They knew that the road ahead would be difficult, but they also knew that courage was not the absence of fear—it was moving forward with hope.
